my_sentence: Today I sent my daughter to school and then we eat something there.
correction: Today I sent my daughter to school, and we ate something there.
explanation: These completed actions are in the past, so use the past-tense verb "ate" to match "sent."
correct_examples: I took my son to school and ate breakfast with him.
We visited the museum and bought lunch there.

my_sentence: If they making a lottery, they will try to save them for their futures.
correction: If they make money in a lottery, they will try to save it for their future.
explanation: Use the simple present after "if" for a real condition, and use the object pronoun "it" for money.
correct_examples: If I earn extra money, I will save it.
If she wins the lottery, she will invest the money.
context: Discussing what poor people might do with unexpected money.

my_sentence: They don't get education, so they don't know how to make right decisions.
correction: They don't get educated, so they don't know how to make the right decisions.
explanation: Use the adjective "educated" after "get," and use the determiner "the" when referring to the relevant decisions.
correct_examples: Children need to get educated before making important decisions.
We should make the right decisions carefully.
context: Explaining why some people make poor choices.

my_sentence: They have enough money to live up their lives.
correction: They have enough money to live out their lives.
explanation: The fixed expression is "live out one's life," meaning to spend the rest of one's life in a particular way.
correct_examples: They want to live out their lives peacefully.
He lived out his final years in the countryside.

my_sentence: Rich people have their successful career and businesses.
correction: Rich people have successful careers and businesses.
explanation: The general statement refers to many people and their careers, so use the plural noun "careers" without the unnecessary possessive determiner.
correct_examples: Successful careers often require years of effort.
They built successful businesses together.

my_sentence: They will have a three free time to do something they want.
correction: They will have free time to do what they want.
explanation: "Free time" is an uncountable phrase, so do not put a number or article before it.
correct_examples: I have some free time this evening.
She uses her free time to read.
context: Discussing the advantages of having money.

my_sentence: If we hold someone on a pedestal, we can't think about their ideas critically.
correction: If we put someone on a pedestal, we can't think about their ideas critically.
explanation: The idiom is "put someone on a pedestal," meaning to admire someone too much.
correct_examples: Don't put celebrities on a pedestal.
She put her manager on a pedestal and ignored his mistakes.
context: Discussing excessive admiration of famous people.

my_sentence: It is like a group of silly person talking about their ideas.
correction: It is like a group of silly people talking about their ideas.
explanation: After "a group of," use the plural count noun "people," not singular "person."
correct_examples: A group of people discussed the plan.
A group of silly people caused trouble.

my_sentence: All the other hand, others will try to keep silent.
correction: On the other hand, others will try to keep silent.
explanation: The contrast linker is the fixed phrase "on the other hand."
correct_examples: On the other hand, some people prefer to stay quiet.
The plan is expensive; on the other hand, it is reliable.

my_sentence: Everyone want to live in the city, so they need to buy a house.
correction: Everyone wants to live in the city, so they need to buy a house.
explanation: The indefinite pronoun "everyone" is grammatically singular, so the verb takes -s: "wants."
correct_examples: Everyone wants a better life.
Everyone needs to follow the rules.

my_sentence: These products are expensive than the others.
correction: These products are more expensive than the others.
explanation: Use "more + adjective" to form the comparative of the multi-syllable adjective "expensive."
correct_examples: This apartment is more expensive than that one.
Online courses are more convenient than books.

my_sentence: Some of my coworkers are fan from some company.
correction: Some of my coworkers are fans of some companies.
explanation: Use plural "fans" after the plural subject, and the correct collocation is "a fan of a company."
correct_examples: Some of my coworkers are fans of Apple.
They are fans of several sports teams.

my_sentence: Someone like to buy Apple product.
correction: Someone likes to buy Apple products.
explanation: The singular subject "someone" takes "likes," and the general noun "products" is plural.
correct_examples: Someone likes to buy new products.
Someone always wants to try the latest model.
context: Talking about people who prefer certain brands.

my_sentence: They more care about their products, not their celebrities.
correction: They care more about their products, not their celebrities.
explanation: In this sentence, the adverb "more" follows the verb phrase: "care more about."
correct_examples: Customers care more about quality than advertisements.
I care more about the product than the celebrity.
context: Explaining why coworkers follow brands rather than celebrities.

my_sentence: After our class, I eat my dinner and rest.
correction: After our class, I ate my dinner and rested.
explanation: The speaker was describing completed actions, so both verbs should be in the past tense.
correct_examples: After class, I ate dinner and went home.
I watched a movie and rested afterward.

my_sentence: You can easy to enter the school.
correction: You can easily enter the school.
explanation: After the modal "can," use the adverb "easily" before the base verb; do not use "easy to" in this structure.
correct_examples: You can easily find the station.
Students can easily apply online.
context: Discussing how money can provide access to schools.

my_sentence: You can fix almost difficulties in your life.
correction: You can face most of the difficulties in your life.
explanation: The natural collocation is "face difficulties"; "most of the difficulties" is also more accurate than "almost difficulties."
correct_examples: Everyone faces difficulties in life.
Money can help you deal with most difficulties.
context: Discussing the advantages of having money.

my_sentence: If they have a health problem, they can find the best hospital.
correction: If they have health problems, they can find the best hospital.
explanation: The general statement refers to health problems in general, so the plural count noun is natural here.
correct_examples: People with health problems need good care.
If she has health problems, she visits a specialist.
context: Explaining how wealth helps with medical care.

my_sentence: If you donate hundreds of million dollars, you can enter the school.
correction: If you donate hundreds of millions of dollars, you can enter the school.
explanation: After "hundreds of," the count noun must be plural: "millions."
correct_examples: The project cost hundreds of millions of dollars.
They donated millions of dollars to the university.

my_sentence: You need to send them to hospital.
correction: You need to send them to a hospital.
explanation: When referring to one hospital as a countable place, use the indefinite article "a."
correct_examples: We took him to a hospital.
She was sent to a hospital for treatment.
context: Discussing medical support for family members.

my_sentence: If they want to finish their study, you need to give them support.
correction: If they want to finish their studies, you need to give them your support.
explanation: Use the plural noun "studies" for a person's education, and the possessive determiner "your" makes the support specific.
correct_examples: She finished her studies abroad.
Parents should give their children support.
context: Discussing the cost of helping family members.

my_sentence: You can get medicine in days or two days.
correction: You can get the medicine within two or three days.
explanation: Use "within + time period" to express a deadline, and include the article when referring to the medicine already mentioned.
correct_examples: The package will arrive within two days.
You can receive the medicine within three days.

my_sentence: If you get opportunity to other cities, you can finish your education there.
correction: If you get the opportunity to go to other cities, you can finish your education there.
explanation: Use the article "the" with this specific opportunity, and add "to go" before the destination phrase.
correct_examples: I got the opportunity to work abroad.
She had the opportunity to go to another city.
context: Discussing opportunities that money can provide.

my_sentence: I miss some opportunities when I graduated from school.
correction: I missed some opportunities when I graduated from school.
explanation: The missed opportunities and graduation are completed past events, so use "missed."
correct_examples: I missed several opportunities after graduation.
She missed the chance to study abroad.
context: Reflecting on missed opportunities after college.

my_sentence: They can train according there to their mistakes.
correction: They can train according to their mistakes.
explanation: The fixed phrase is "according to," followed directly by the relevant noun phrase.
correct_examples: The teacher adjusted the lesson according to our mistakes.
We train according to the results.

my_sentence: You expect he or she to become your employee.
correction: You expect him or her to become your employee.
explanation: After the verb "expect," use an object pronoun: "expect him or her to..."
correct_examples: We expect him to finish the work.
They expect her to become a good manager.

my_sentence: If someone are poor, he or she has to work hard.
correction: If someone is poor, he or she has to work hard.
explanation: The indefinite pronoun "someone" is singular, so use "is," not "are."
correct_examples: If someone is poor, they may need support.
Someone is waiting outside.

my_sentence: They can't get out of poverty.
correction: They can get out of poverty.
explanation: The teacher was describing a possible way to escape poverty, so the modal must be positive: "can get out."
correct_examples: Education can help people get out of poverty.
With support, families can improve their lives.

my_sentence: The government will provided it for you freely.
correction: The government will provide it for you freely.
explanation: After the modal "will," use the base form "provide," not the past participle "provided."
correct_examples: The government will provide support.
The service will provide free medicine.

my_sentence: Even though their family was good, they can become bad.
correction: Even though his or her family is good, he or she can become bad.
explanation: The singular person needs matching singular pronouns, and a general present condition uses "is" and "can become."
correct_examples: Even if his family is wealthy, he can make bad choices.
A person can change even if their family is supportive.
context: Discussing whether wealthy people become unethical.

my_sentence: They have more ethical.
correction: They have better ethics or morals.
explanation: "Ethical" is an adjective; after "have," use the noun "ethics" or "morals."
correct_examples: The company has strong ethics.
Good leaders should have sound morals.
context: Discussing whether wealth makes people morally better.

my_sentence: He or she can be spender money.
correction: He or she can spend money.
explanation: After the modal "can," use the base verb "spend." "Spender" is a noun, not a verb.
correct_examples: They can spend money to solve the problem.
She can spend more if necessary.
context: Discussing how wealthy people may respond to threats.

my_sentence: In reality he defeat other competitors.
correction: In reality, he defeats other competitors.
explanation: This is a general description of what he does, so use the third-person singular present form "defeats."
correct_examples: In reality, she defeats stronger competitors.
He defeats his rivals through hard work.
